'''Margaret Hilary Millington''' (22 March 1944 &ndash; 5 March 1973) was an English-born mathematician.<ref name="standrews" />

She was born '''Margaret Hilary Ashworth''' in [[Halifax, Yorkshire]], the daughter of the local assistant head postmaster. She was an undergraduate at [[St Mary's College, Durham]] and earned her PhD at the [[University of Oxford]], where she was supervised by [[A. O. L. Atkin]].<ref name="lms" /><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=147693}}</ref> 

In 1968, she married Lieutenant A.H. Millington, an officer in the [[Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers]].<ref name="lms" /><ref name="standrews" /> She was awarded a two-year Science Research Council Fellowship which allowed her to pursue research at any university. During her husband's two-year posting in Germany, she taught mathematics at an Army Education Centre there.<ref name="standrews" />

She died in Germany due to a [[brain tumour]] at the age of 28.<ref name="lms">{{cite journal |last=Atkin |first=A. O. L. |date=September 1985 |title=Obituary: Margaret Hilary Millington (née Ashworth) |journal=Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society |publisher=London Mathematical Society |volume=17 |issue=5 |pages=484–486 |doi=10.1112/blms/17.5.484|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Although her career was cut short, in 1983, the [[London Mathematical Society]] organized a symposium on [[modular form]]s. During the symposium, the importance of her doctoral thesis and post-doctoral research became clear. The work that she had started during her fellowship was picked up and pursued by other mathematicians, leading to a resurgence in the field.<ref name="standrews" /> Her research had dealt with [[modular forms]], as well as [[subgroups]] of the [[modular group]].<ref name="standrews" />

In a tribute to Millington, Atkin said "I have no doubt that, had she lived, she would have made exciting original contributions to a field which has at last come into its own again, after nearly a quarter century in the doldrums, and where there are now at least twenty first rate people of her generation working actively."<ref name="standrews">{{cite web |last1=O'Connor |first1=John J. |last2=Robertson |first2=Edmund F. |date=February 2010 |title=Margaret Hilary Ashworth Millington |url=http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Biographies/Millington.html |website=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]] |publisher=School of Mathematics and Statistics, University of St Andrews, Scotland}}</ref>
